programme: MSX1, CDX1, PAX2, HOXD10 and HOXA13 belong to the Cdx-Hox-Pax2 posterior/urogenital patterning network: CDX1 sets collinear posterior Hox expression, HOXA13/HOXD10 specify caudal Müllerian-duct identity (uterus/cervix/vagina), PAX2 marks and maintains Müllerian-derived epithelium, and MSX1 acts alongside this BMP/WNT-linked homeodomain code in organ patterning.
role_in_a: Not established as a network in Alzheimer's disease; only HOXD10 has direct evidence, via a miR-10b-5p/HOXD10 axis reported to modulate pathology in a rat model. MSX1, CDX1, PAX2 and HOXA13 carry no disease-specific evidence in the retrieved record beyond generic Open Targets percentiles, so any role here (e.g. re-expression of a silenced developmental identity programme in stressed or degenerating neurons) is inferred, not documented.
role_in_b: This is the module pathologists already use: PAX2 expression is a standard marker retained in endometrioid endometrial carcinoma (and lost in serous carcinoma), its estrogen/progesterone-regulated promoter methylation is documented, MSX1 is proposed as a marker for uterus-preserving therapy of endometrioid carcinoma, and HOXD10 methylation tracks early-onset endometrial cancer. The network functions here to maintain/mark Müllerian epithelial lineage identity in the tumor.
shared_axis: If real, the shared axis would be reuse of an embryonic organ-identity homeobox toolkit that is normally silenced after development: retained/re-expressed to hold epithelial lineage identity in endometrioid tumor cells, and aberrantly reactivated as part of a broader loss of developmental gene silencing proposed in neurodegeneration. This is a shared-mechanism-type story, not a shared-complex one — the two diseases would not be using the same physical pathway, only the same class of dormant regulatory network.
reasoning: The module itself is real and nameable — PAX2/HOXA13/HOXD10/MSX1/CDX1 form a recognized developmental patterning network and three of them are independently and strongly placed in endometrioid cancer. But nothing in the record connects this network to Alzheimer's disease except one indirect rodent miRNA study for a single member (HOXD10), and brain vs. endometrium is not a pairing anatomy or clinical practice would suggest on its own, so the account rests on reasoning about developmental-gene reactivation rather than retrieved evidence.
support: 39075663 (PAX2 retained expression marks MMR-deficient endometrioid carcinoma); 38185904 (PAX2 regulated by estrogen/progesterone via promoter methylation in endometrioid adenocarcinoma); 32630554 (MSX1 proposed marker for uterus-preserving therapy of endometrioid carcinoma); 30850842 (HOXD10 among genes in genome-wide methylation profile of early-onset endometrial cancer); 33307856 (HOXD10 up-regulation via miR-10b-5p inhibition attenuates AD pathology in rats)
how_to_falsify: Profile chromatin accessibility/expression of the HOXA13/HOXD10/PAX2/MSX1/CDX1 loci (e.g. ATAC-seq or RNA-seq) in postmortem AD hippocampus/cortex versus age-matched controls; if none of these loci show differential accessibility or expression beyond HOXD10's already-reported change, the 'reactivated developmental network' account has no basis beyond the one gene already known, and the pairing should be dropped.
caveats: Tissue pairing is anatomically distant (brain vs. uterine endometrium) with no stated clinical comorbidity link. The 96 patient-group comparisons come from only 6 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance fractions (e.g. MSX1 66/96) reflect far less independent replication than the raw count suggests. Other homeobox/developmental factors (PITX2, SIX3, NPAS1, NR6A1) appear in the single-view exclusion list, meaning the homeobox theme was not dominant across most individual patient groups, only in the aggregate. Tissue-generic exclusion of SOX10, NOTCH1, RFX5, STAT4 removed the obvious neural-crest/immune master regulators, which is why GATA3 and NFKBIB (both with real single-disease literature: GATA3 in endometrioid, none for NFKBIB) were not built into the carrying set — they don't mechanistically connect to the HOX/PAX2 patterning story despite being retained after filtering. No paper in the record addresses both diseases jointly through any factor.
